name: Huberman Sleep Protocol
summary: Morning light exposure + evening wind-down for optimal circadian rhythm

actions.name: Morning sunlight (10 min)
actions.description: Get 10 minutes of direct sunlight within 30 minutes of waking. Go outside — window glass blocks beneficial wavelengths. No sunglasses. Cloudy days need 20-30 minutes.

actions.name: Afternoon sunlight (optional)
actions.description: Brief afternoon sun exposure helps anchor circadian rhythm. Even 5-10 minutes helps.

actions.name: Dim lights after sunset
actions.description: Reduce overhead lights after sunset. Use lamps at eye level or below. Dimmer is better. This signals your brain that night is coming.

actions.name: Enable night mode on screens
actions.description: Turn on night shift / warm colors on all devices. Reduces blue light that suppresses melatonin.

actions.name: No screens 1hr before bed
actions.description: Put away phone, laptop, TV. Read a physical book, do gentle stretching, or relaxation exercises. This is the hardest one but most impactful.

actions.name: Cool bedroom (65-68°F)
actions.description: Body temperature needs to drop for sleep. Keep bedroom cool. Consider a warm shower 1-2 hours before bed (counterintuitive but helps cooling after).

actions.name: Wake at consistent time
actions.description: Wake up at the same time every day, including weekends. This anchors your circadian rhythm. Consistency beats duration.

notes: Start with morning light — it's the highest impact. Add other actions gradually. Don't try to be perfect on day 1.
